🇵🇭🇮🇩 ANCIENT SEAFARERS MASTERED OCEAN TRAVEL 40,000 YEARS AGO 

A groundbreaking study proves ancient people in Southeast Asia were skilled sailors 40,000 years ago, far earlier than believed possible.

Stone tools discovered in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Timor-Leste reveal evidence of plant processing used to extract fibers for ropes, nets, and bindings essential for boatbuilding and deep-sea fishing. 

Combined with fishing hooks and remnants of tuna and sharks, these sites show a sophisticated maritime society.

The findings challenge the belief that technological advancement was centered only in Africa and Europe. 

These prehistoric explorers weren't drifting on bamboo rafts by accident. 

They were highly skilled navigators with the knowledge and technology to cross deep oceans.

Their boat-building expertise likely made the region a hub for maritime innovation that still flourishes today.

Source: Express US

🇹🇷 ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER 2,200-YEAR-OLD NECROPOLIS IN BIBLICAL CITY OF COLOSSAE

Excavators in Turkey just discovered over 60 ancient tombs in Colossae, the city where St. Paul wrote his Epistle to the Colossians in the New Testament.

Archaeologist Baris Yener:

"This is the largest necropolis in Anatolia featuring rock-cut, trough-shaped tombs. 

The findings reveal how much the people of Colossae valued magic, talismans and objects believed to have protective powers."

The pre-Christian tombs contain oil lamps (to illuminate the afterlife journey), healing stones, amulets, coins, sandals, terracotta ceramics, and glass bottles. 

Ancient residents carved graves directly into travertine rock to preserve farmland for grain production.

Colossae was destroyed by earthquakes in the 1st and 8th centuries AD and abandoned. 

Now it's revealing how people worshipped before Christianity arrived.

Source: Fox News / Anadolu Agency
